origin.description: Equi-tailed two-sided intervals from the normal approximation to a statistic.
origin.usage:
norm.ci(boot.out = NULL, conf = 0.95, index = 1, var.t0 = NULL,
        t0 = NULL, t = NULL, L = NULL, h = function(t) t,
        hdot = function(t) 1, hinv = function(t) t)

arguments.name: boot.out
arguments.text: A bootstrap object. Required when t0 is omitted, and also when both var.t0 and t are omitted.

arguments.name: conf
arguments.text: One confidence level, or several.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based position of the statistic in the bootstrap output. Unused when boot.out is omitted.

arguments.name: var.t0
arguments.text: Variance of the statistic. If omitted, the sample variance of t is used. With a transformation, a supplied variance is scaled by hdot(t0)^2 before h is applied.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Observed statistic. Taken from boot.out when omitted.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates. They estimate the variance when var.t0 is omitted, and they estimate the bias whenever they are supplied.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values for the untransformed statistic. Used for the variance only when both var.t0 and t are omitted.

arguments.name: h
arguments.text: Monotone transformation. The interval is calculated on the scale of h and mapped back by hinv. The default is the identity.

arguments.name: hdot
arguments.text: Derivative of h. The default is the constant function 1.

arguments.name: hinv
arguments.text: Inverse of h. If h is supplied and hinv is not, the interval stays on the transformed scale.

origin.details: The interval has half-width qnorm((1+conf)/2) * sqrt(var.t0). When replicates are supplied it is centered at 2*h(t0) - mean(h(t)); otherwise it is centered at h(t0). The variance from L is sum((hdot(t0) * L / length(L))^2). The manual says a single confidence level is returned as a vector. The installed function builds the result with cbind, so one level is still a one-row matrix.
origin.value: A matrix with one row per confidence level and three columns: the level and the two endpoints. A single level is still that one-row matrix.
origin.example:
library(boot)
hours <- c(3, 5, 7, 18, 43, 85, 91, 98, 100, 130, 230, 487)
air.mean <- mean(hours)
air.n <- length(hours)
air.v <- air.mean^2 / air.n
print(norm.ci(t0 = air.mean, var.t0 = air.v))
print(exp(norm.ci(t0 = log(air.mean), var.t0 = 1/air.n)[, 2:3]))

translation.description: Equi-tailed two-sided intervals from the normal approximation to a statistic.
translation.usage: norm_ci(boot_out=None, conf=0.95, index=1, var_t0=None, t0=None, t=None, L=None, h=None, hdot=None, hinv=None)

arguments.name: boot_out
arguments.text: Optional bootstrap object with t0 and t. Required when t0 is omitted.

arguments.name: conf
arguments.text: One confidence level, or several.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based position of the statistic. Unused when boot_out is omitted.

arguments.name: var_t0
arguments.text: Variance of the statistic. If omitted, the sample variance of t is used. A supplied variance is scaled by hdot(t0)^2.

arguments.name: t0
arguments.text: Observed statistic. Taken from boot_out when omitted.

arguments.name: t
arguments.text: Bootstrap replicates. They estimate the variance when var_t0 is omitted, and the bias whenever they are supplied.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values for the untransformed statistic. Used for the variance only when both var_t0 and t are omitted.

arguments.name: h
arguments.text: Monotone transformation. None is the identity.

arguments.name: hdot
arguments.text: Derivative of h. None is the constant 1.

arguments.name: hinv
arguments.text: Inverse of h. None is the identity.

translation.details: The half-width is qnorm((1+conf)/2) * sqrt(var_t0), with qnorm in pure Python. Replicates center the interval at 2*h(t0) - mean(h(t)). The variance from L is the sum of squared scaled influence values. One confidence level is still one row of a three-column matrix, matching cbind in the installed function. The sample variance divides by n - 1.
translation.value: A NumPy array with one row per confidence level and three columns: the level and the two endpoints.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from boot.ci import norm_ci

hours = np.array([3, 5, 7, 18, 43, 85, 91, 98, 100, 130, 230, 487], dtype=float)
air_mean = float(np.mean(hours))
air_n = hours.size
air_v = air_mean ** 2 / air_n
print(norm_ci(t0=air_mean, var_t0=air_v))
logged = norm_ci(t0=math.log(air_mean), var_t0=1.0 / air_n)
print(np.exp(logged[0, 1:]))
